questions.stem: A student studies a mutant strain of Escherichia coli. She measures beta-galactosidase activity (relative units) in four growth media. Glucose, no lactose: wild type 1, mutant 1. Glucose plus lactose: wild type 2, mutant 1. No glucose, lactose present: wild type 100, mutant 2. No glucose, lactose present, and cAMP added to the medium: wild type 100, mutant 95. Which mutation best explains these results?
choices: Loss of function of the lac repressor
Loss of the ability of CAP to bind cAMP
Loss of adenylyl cyclase activity
Nonsense mutation in the lacZ gene
Operator change that blocks repressor binding
questions.explanation: The lac operon needs **lactose** (to release the repressor) and **low glucose**, when **cAMP** rises and the **cAMP-CAP complex** helps RNA polymerase bind the promoter. The mutant cannot turn the operon on, but added cAMP restores it, so the cell cannot make its own cAMP: **adenylyl cyclase** is missing. A CAP defect is the tempting choice, but then extra cAMP would not help, because CAP could not bind it. Repressor or operator defects would increase expression, not block it, and a lacZ nonsense mutation would not respond to cAMP.
questions.explanation_pt: O operon lac precisa de **lactose** (para soltar o repressor) e de **glicose baixa**, quando o **cAMP** sobe e o **complexo cAMP-CAP** ajuda a RNA polimerase a se ligar ao promotor. O mutante não consegue ativar o operon, mas o cAMP adicionado o restaura; portanto, a célula não produz seu próprio cAMP: falta a **adenilato ciclase**. Um defeito da CAP é a alternativa tentadora, mas nesse caso o cAMP extra não ajudaria, pois a CAP não conseguiria ligá-lo. Defeitos do repressor ou do operador aumentariam a expressão, em vez de bloqueá-la, e uma mutação sem sentido no lacZ não responderia ao cAMP.

questions.stem: An investigator studies a temperature-sensitive mutant of Escherichia coli. She grows it at the restrictive temperature and analyzes newly made DNA. Results: leading-strand synthesis, normal; lagging strand, many short pieces of about 1,500 nucleotides; short RNA segments, still attached at the 5' end of each piece; replication fork movement, normal. Which enzyme activity is most likely defective?
choices: 5'→3' exonuclease of DNA polymerase I
Nick sealing by DNA ligase
RNA primer synthesis by primase
5'→3' polymerase of DNA polymerase III
Supercoil relief by DNA gyrase
questions.explanation: Each **Okazaki fragment** starts with an RNA primer. The **5'→3' exonuclease of DNA polymerase I** removes that primer and fills the gap with DNA; here the primers stay attached, so this step failed. **DNA ligase** is the tempting choice: a ligase defect also leaves short fragments, but their primers would already be replaced by DNA, leaving only unsealed nicks. Primase, polymerase III or gyrase defects would stop fragment synthesis or fork movement.
questions.explanation_pt: Cada **fragmento de Okazaki** começa com um primer de RNA. A **exonuclease 5'→3' da DNA polimerase I** remove esse primer e preenche a lacuna com DNA; aqui os primers continuam ligados, então essa etapa falhou. A **DNA ligase** é a alternativa tentadora: um defeito da ligase também deixa fragmentos curtos, mas seus primers já estariam substituídos por DNA, restando apenas quebras (*nicks*) não seladas. Defeitos da primase, da polimerase III ou da girase impediriam a síntese dos fragmentos ou o avanço da forquilha.

questions.stem: A researcher treats cultured human cells with nitrous acid. This chemical removes the amino group from cytosine and turns it into uracil inside the DNA. Without repair, each such change becomes a C:G to T:A mutation after replication. The cells repair most of these lesions within hours, and each repair replaces only one nucleotide. Which enzyme performs the first step of this repair?
choices: AP endonuclease
MSH2 mismatch-recognition protein
Nucleotide excision endonuclease
DNA glycosylase
DNA ligase III
questions.explanation: Cytosine **deamination** makes uracil, a single damaged base that does not distort the helix, so it is fixed by **base excision repair**. A **DNA glycosylase** (here uracil-DNA glycosylase) acts first: it cuts the bond between the base and the sugar and leaves an **AP site**. **AP endonuclease** is the tempting choice, but it acts second, cutting the backbone at the empty site; polymerase and ligase then finish the repair. Mismatch repair fixes replication errors, and nucleotide excision repair removes bulky lesions such as UV dimers.
questions.explanation_pt: A **desaminação** da citosina forma uracila, uma base lesada isolada que não distorce a hélice; por isso, é corrigida pelo **reparo por excisão de bases**. Uma **DNA glicosilase** (aqui, a uracila-DNA glicosilase) age primeiro: ela corta a ligação entre a base e o açúcar e deixa um **sítio AP**. A **AP endonuclease** é a alternativa tentadora, mas age em segundo lugar, cortando o esqueleto de açúcar-fosfato no sítio vazio; a polimerase e a ligase completam o reparo. O reparo de erros de pareamento corrige erros da replicação, e o reparo por excisão de nucleotídeos remove lesões volumosas, como os dímeros causados por UV.

questions.stem: A researcher compares normal skin fibroblasts with cells from a squamous cell carcinoma. The fibroblasts stop dividing after about 50 divisions, and their chromosome ends get shorter with each division. The cancer cells keep dividing, and the length of their chromosome ends stays stable. An enzyme that is active in the cancer cells, but not in the fibroblasts, explains the difference. Which feature allows this enzyme to keep the chromosome ends long?
choices: It removes RNA primers with a 5'→3' exonuclease
It copies an RNA template that is part of the enzyme
It seals nicks between Okazaki fragments
It relieves supercoiling by cutting both DNA strands
It extends the 5' end of the lagging strand from a primer
questions.explanation: Most cancers reactivate **telomerase**, a **reverse transcriptase** that carries its own **RNA template**. It adds TTAGGG repeats to the **3' end** of the chromosome, which replaces the DNA lost when the last lagging-strand primer is removed. The tempting choice about the 5' end is wrong because no DNA polymerase can add nucleotides to a 5' end; telomerase extends the 3' overhang, and primase and DNA polymerase then fill in the complementary strand. Primer removal, nick sealing and supercoil relief are normal replication steps that do not prevent shortening.
questions.explanation_pt: A maioria dos cânceres reativa a **telomerase**, uma **transcriptase reversa** que carrega seu próprio **molde de RNA**. Ela adiciona repetições TTAGGG à **extremidade 3'** do cromossomo, o que repõe o DNA perdido quando o último primer da fita descontínua é removido. A alternativa sobre a extremidade 5' é tentadora, mas está errada, porque nenhuma DNA polimerase adiciona nucleotídeos a uma extremidade 5'; a telomerase estende a extremidade 3' saliente, e a primase e a DNA polimerase depois completam a fita complementar. Remoção de primers, selagem de quebras e alívio do superenrolamento são etapas normais da replicação que não impedem o encurtamento.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man has cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides) with itchy red plaques on his trunk. His disease has progressed despite several earlier systemic treatments. He starts oral vorinostat. Which change is most likely to occur in the tumor cells?
choices: Increased methylation of CpG islands near promoters
Tighter histone-DNA binding with more heterochromatin
Loss of acetyl groups from histone lysine residues
Double-strand DNA breaks from trapped topoisomerase II
More histone acetylation and looser, active chromatin
questions.explanation: **Histone deacetylase inhibitors** such as vorinostat keep acetyl groups on histone **lysines**. Acetylation removes their positive charge, so histones bind DNA less tightly; chromatin opens (**euchromatin**) and silenced genes, including tumor suppressors, can be transcribed again. Tighter binding with more heterochromatin is the tempting choice, but that is the effect of deacetylation, the step the drug blocks. CpG methylation silences genes and is a separate mark; trapped topoisomerase II is how etoposide works.
questions.explanation_pt: **Inibidores de histona desacetilase**, como o vorinostate, mantêm grupos acetil nas **lisinas** das histonas. A acetilação remove a carga positiva delas, de modo que as histonas se ligam ao DNA com menos força; a cromatina se abre (**eucromatina**) e genes silenciados, incluindo supressores de tumor, podem voltar a ser transcritos. Ligação mais forte com mais heterocromatina é a alternativa tentadora, mas esse é o efeito da desacetilação, a etapa que o fármaco bloqueia. A metilação de CpG silencia genes e é uma marca separada; aprisionar a topoisomerase II é o mecanismo do etoposídeo.

questions.stem: A 5-month-old girl has spinal muscular atrophy. Genetic testing shows that both copies of SMN1 are deleted and that she has two copies of the nearby SMN2 gene. SMN2 differs from SMN1 by a single base change in exon 7, which causes most SMN2 transcripts to lose exon 7. She is treated with nusinersen, given by intrathecal injection. How does this drug most likely increase functional SMN protein?
choices: It delivers a working SMN1 gene in a viral vector
It lets ribosomes read through an early stop codon
It binds SMN2 pre-mRNA so that exon 7 is kept
It removes methyl groups from the SMN2 promoter
It destroys mutant SMN1 mRNA by RNA interference
questions.explanation: **Nusinersen** is an **antisense oligonucleotide**. It binds a site in SMN2 pre-mRNA that normally tells the **spliceosome** to skip exon 7, so more transcripts keep exon 7 and make full-length, working SMN protein. Gene therapy with a viral vector is the tempting choice, but that is a different drug (onasemnogene abeparvovec), which adds a new SMN1 gene; nusinersen is a short oligonucleotide and adds no gene. Both SMN1 copies are deleted, so the drug cannot act on an SMN1 stop codon or SMN1 mRNA.
questions.explanation_pt: A **nusinersena** é um **oligonucleotídeo antissenso**. Ela se liga a um sítio do pré-mRNA do SMN2 que normalmente faz o **spliceossomo** excluir o éxon 7; assim, mais transcritos mantêm o éxon 7 e produzem proteína SMN completa e funcional. A terapia gênica com vetor viral é a alternativa tentadora, mas corresponde a outro fármaco (onasemnogeno abeparvoveque), que adiciona um novo gene SMN1; a nusinersena é um oligonucleotídeo curto e não adiciona nenhum gene. As duas cópias do SMN1 estão deletadas, então o fármaco não pode agir sobre um códon de parada ou um mRNA do SMN1.

questions.stem: A 14-month-old boy has large bruises after minor falls and a swollen, painful knee. His maternal uncle had a similar bleeding disorder. Laboratory results: platelet count 260,000/mm3 (normal); PT 12 seconds (normal); aPTT 74 seconds (prolonged); factor VIII activity normal; factor IX activity below 1%. Sequencing of the factor IX gene finds one base change inside an exon: on the coding strand, a TGG codon (tryptophan) has become TGA. Which description best fits this mutation?
choices: Silent mutation; the same amino acid is still inserted
Missense mutation; another amino acid replaces tryptophan
Frameshift mutation; every later codon is changed
Nonsense mutation; translation ends early at this codon
Splice-site mutation; part of an intron stays in the mRNA
questions.explanation: The boy has **hemophilia B** (X-linked factor IX deficiency). On the coding strand TGA matches the mRNA codon **UGA**, a **stop codon**, so this is a **nonsense mutation**: translation ends early and the short protein (and often the mRNA) is destroyed. Missense is the tempting choice because only one base changed, but a single-base change that creates a stop codon is a nonsense mutation. No bases were added or lost, so the reading frame is intact, and the change is inside an exon, not at a splice site.
questions.explanation_pt: O menino tem **hemofilia B** (deficiência de fator IX ligada ao X). Na fita codificadora, TGA corresponde ao códon **UGA** do mRNA, um **códon de parada**; portanto, trata-se de uma **mutação sem sentido** (*nonsense*): a tradução termina cedo, e a proteína curta (e muitas vezes o mRNA) é destruída. A mutação de sentido trocado (*missense*) é a alternativa tentadora, pois só uma base mudou, mas uma troca de base única que cria um códon de parada é uma mutação sem sentido. Nenhuma base foi adicionada ou perdida, então a fase de leitura está intacta, e a troca fica dentro de um éxon, não em um sítio de splicing.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with metastatic colon cancer starts treatment with irinotecan. Eight days after the first dose he has severe watery diarrhea, and his neutrophil count is low. The active form of this drug kills tumor cells mainly when they are copying their DNA in S phase. What is the mechanism of action of this drug?
choices: It traps topoisomerase I so DNA single-strand breaks stay open
It traps topoisomerase II so DNA double-strand breaks stay open
It inhibits thymidylate synthase and lowers thymidine supply
It forms cross-links between guanine bases on DNA strands
It binds tubulin and prevents the mitotic spindle from forming
questions.explanation: **Irinotecan** (a camptothecin) binds the **topoisomerase I**-DNA complex after the enzyme has cut one strand and blocks resealing. When a replication fork reaches the trapped complex, the single-strand break becomes a lethal double-strand break, so the drug acts in **S phase**; diarrhea and myelosuppression are its main toxicities. Topoisomerase II is the tempting choice, but that is the target of **etoposide**, which leaves double-strand breaks. Thymidylate synthase is the target of fluorouracil, guanine cross-links come from platinum drugs, and tubulin binding is how vinca alkaloids act.
questions.explanation_pt: O **irinotecano** (uma camptotecina) se liga ao complexo **topoisomerase I**-DNA depois que a enzima cortou uma fita e impede a religação. Quando uma forquilha de replicação chega ao complexo aprisionado, a quebra de fita simples vira uma quebra de fita dupla letal; por isso, o fármaco age na **fase S**, e diarreia e mielossupressão são suas principais toxicidades. A topoisomerase II é a alternativa tentadora, mas é o alvo do **etoposídeo**, que deixa quebras de fita dupla. A timidilato sintase é o alvo da fluoruracila, as ligações cruzadas entre guaninas vêm dos derivados de platina, e a ligação à tubulina é o mecanismo dos alcaloides da vinca.
